run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 14 of the usual 15 holdings. Intuitive Surgical wasn't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the company itself.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly and is sitting well below its highs for the year, but defense budgets keep flowing steadily, so nothing has really changed about the underlying business.

ASML.sentence: ASML is down a touch and off its peak, which is just the normal ebb and flow for the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases on long-term contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is pretty much the whole, dependable story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft slipped a touch but has actually held up far better than the other big tech names lately — the Azure cloud and AI story keeps grinding along without drama while investors treat it as the safe place to hide.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher — the company that sells lab equipment and supplies to basically every biotech and research lab — is basically flat and sitting right near its yearly high, so there's no bargain here and not much new happening.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is roughly flat today; its profits look fat right now mostly because fighting involving Iran has pushed oil prices well above normal, which is the oil price doing the work, not the business getting better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow dropped sharply and is now down nearly half from its high, a much bigger fall than a passing dip — but big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant software on long contracts, so the business story and the stock story have diverged.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore jumped over 5% and is outrunning other copper miners, as investors give extra credit to its commodity-trading arm, which makes money from market swings on top of what the mines dig up.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta eased back slightly, but the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still creeping steadily upward — the headline price looked soft only because of which products sold, not because the business weakened.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA edged up, though a weakening Mexican peso works against it since most of its sales as the big Latin American Coke bottler come in pesos that convert to fewer dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber slipped a bit, but people keep booking more rides and food orders through the app — the open question is still whether the self-driving-car companies choose to run on Uber's app or go it alone, which is a worry about the future, not a problem today.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is roughly flat and trading for less than its ships would cost to replace — the Danish shipping giant is the kind of trade-dependent, up-and-down business that often looks cheapest right when global shipping is in a lull.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is steady, and it's trading unusually close to rival Visa despite no particular problem of its own — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so this is a mood story, not a business one.

ISRG.sentence: Intuitive Surgical didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell about 6% after Amazon and Google's parent showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are exactly the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
